descriptions.l0: There is not enough material to confirm who runs this relay, so no conclusion is made about whether it keeps user content.
descriptions.l1: The operator is confirmed, but the public statements are not enough to judge whether content is kept by default or for how long.
descriptions.l2: The operator is confirmed, and a public policy states a retention period, a condition for keeping content, or a deletion rule.
descriptions.l3: The operator is confirmed, and a public policy says user content is not kept by default.
descriptions.l4: The public policy says user content is not kept by default, and a public third-party report or Folkbench review states the scope and limits of that check.

methods.cacheBody: Splits the 2M input tokens into cache hits (billed at published cache-read price, or input price when unquoted) and cache misses, plus 40k output tokens, so long-context coding sessions reflect real cache discounts.
methods.compareBody: Normalizes probe retention, first-token latency, session cost, cache discount, and 24-hour availability across all published routes of the selected model (0–100), and weights them according to the chosen priority focus.
methods.description: Ranking performance, data security, degradation monitoring, and host reachability measure distinct dimensions.
methods.frontierBody: Plots coding session cost (2M input + 40k output tokens, log scale) against Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5. The Pareto frontier highlights routes where no peer is both cheaper and higher-scoring; degradation-adjusted mode scales scores by measured probe retention and 24-hour availability.
methods.hostBody: After saving, the app can check HTTP reachability and latency for the target URL. This does not send your Key or prove that the model works.
methods.integrityBody: Identity probes are sent to relays for each model within the same time window, and raw probe agreement, input tokens, reasoning tokens, and model fingerprints are published directly with no pass/fail verdict.
methods.keyBody: Only a model request made with your own Key can confirm authorization, balance, and model response. This version never starts a potentially billable request automatically.
methods.rankingBody: Public rankings sort by data security level first, then compare 24-hour availability (with 95% Wilson confidence intervals and within-tier rank ranges), time to first token, stability, or session cost.
methods.securityBody: Data security levels (0–4) rate whether the operator is verified and what public retention policies or review notes say, independently of live latency or availability.
methods.title: About checks
